jp.label: JP CPI
jp.source_note: Statistics Bureau of Japan CPI via e-Stat (2020-base, table 0003427113, NSA; medium-group/中分類 partition)
jp.weight_note: weights = static 2020-base CPI medium-group weights (per 10000), renormalised monthly
notes: the Bank of Japan publishes a 10% trimmed mean, a weighted median and a mode, and they are overlaid here -- but the Bank trims the cross-section of *twelve-month* changes while this engine trims the monthly one, so the two are the same measure in spirit and not the same calculation
the narrowest cross-section on the site: 47 medium groups with rent at 18% of the basket, so an 8% tail is on average barely five components and half of it is whichever single component leads it

series.label: Hospitals
series.note: BEA prices hospital care from this PPI rather than the CPI, and counts what insurers pay rather than what a household is billed.

series.label: Offices of physicians
series.note: Same: the physician-services deflator is PPI-sourced.

series.label: Direct health and medical insurance carriers
series.note: PCE values insurance at the carriers' margin; this PPI is that margin. The CPI has no comparable line.

series.label: Portfolio management
series.note: Portfolio management and investment advice: a PCE line with no CPI counterpart at all, so PPI is its only monthly input.

series.label: Scheduled passenger air transportation
series.note: Air fares are priced differently in the two gauges; the PPI is closer to what PCE does.
